newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CGS Foods says sugar to boost H1 shr.
newsitem.headline: CGS Foods says sugar to boost H1 shr.

text.p: South African food holdings group C.G. Smith Foods Ltd (CGS Foods) said on Wednesday it expected further real earnings growth in the year ahead provided 1996 consumer spending levels were maintained.

It said in a statement accompanying its results for the year to end-September that a number of its subsidiaries were well positioned to lift earnings in the first six months of the 1996/97 financial year.

"The record 1996/97 sugar crop will ensure Illovo produces good results...The Adcock Ingram Ltd merger holds much promise for the future with some early benefits anticipated in the year ahead," its said.
Adcock earlier this year merged its operations with rival pharmaceutical company Premier Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
Subsidiaries Tiger Oats Ltd and ICS Holdings Ltd were well placed in their respective sectors to take full advantage of the economic environment, CGS Foods said.
"Provided consumer spending is maintained at similar levels to 1996, further real growth in (group) earnings should be achieved in the year ahead."
CGS Foods lifted year earnings per share to 525.1 cents from 414.6 cents previously. Attributable income rose to 639.8 million rand from 392.0 million rand.
